body.translated_text: Now, the duties of the <s>varṇa</s> (social class) and <s>āśrama</s> (stage of life).
The four <s>varṇas</s> are born from the mouth, arms, thighs, and feet: the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, <s>Kṣatriya</s>, <s>Vaiśya</s>, and <s>Śūdra</s>.

body.text: yasmād brāhmaṇo asya mukham \āsīd iti śrutiḥ.
body.translated_text: For the <s>Śruti</s> (revealed scripture) says, "The <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> was His mouth."
For the first three, the <s>saṃskāras</s> (sacraments) beginning with the impregnation rite are prescribed.
For these twice-born ones there is the right to the <s>Veda</s>.
Therefore for the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> there are six acts: studying, teaching, sacrificing for oneself, officiating at sacrifices, giving, and receiving gifts.
For the <s>Kṣatriya</s> and <s>Vaiśya</s> there are sacrificing, studying, and giving.
For the <s>Kṣatriya</s> there are protecting the people, restraining the wicked, and warfare.
For the <s>Vaiśya</s> there are cattle-rearing, money-lending, and trade.
For the <s>Śūdra</s> there are service to the twice-born and agriculture.

body.text: brāhmaṇasya-āśramāś catvāraḥ kṣatriyasya-ādyās trayo vaiśyasya dvāv eva.
body.translated_text: The <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> has four <s>āśramas</s>, the <s>Kṣatriya</s> the first three, the <s>Vaiśya</s> only two.

body.text: tad.āśramiṇaś catvāro brahmacārī gṛhasthovānaprastho bhikṣur iti.
body.translated_text: The members of those <s>āśramas</s> are four: the <s>brahmacārī</s> (celibate student), the <s>gṛhastha</s> (householder), the <s>vānaprastha</s> (forest-dweller), and the <s>bhikṣu</s> (mendicant).

body.text: upanīto brahmacārīmekhalā.upavīta.ajina.daṇḍa.dhārī snātvā tarpaṇaṃ brahmayajñaṃ sāyaṃ.prātaḥ sandhyā.upāsana.samidd.homau cakurvan guroḥ pādāv upasaṃgṛhya nitya.abhivandī vratena-adhyayanaṃ \karoti.
body.translated_text: The initiated <s>brahmacārī</s>, wearing the girdle, sacred thread, antelope-skin, and staff, having bathed, performs the libation, the <s>brahmayajña</s> (sacrifice to Brahman), worship of the twilights at evening and dawn, and the kindling-stick oblation; grasping the feet of his teacher and saluting him constantly, he carries out his study with discipline.

body.text: sthite gurau stheyād utthite pūrvam utthāyavrajantam \anugacched. āsīne śayāne ca niyukto nīcair anvāsana.śayane \kuryād.
body.translated_text: When the teacher stands, he should stand; when the teacher rises, he should rise first; he should follow the departing teacher; when the teacher is seated or lying down, being directed, he should make his own seat and bed lower.
Unbidden, he should not perform any act whatever.
Yet even unbidden he should perform his private recitation and his daily duties.

Avoiding hot-water bathing, tooth-cleaning, collyrium, ointment, perfume, flowers, sandals, parasol, daytime sleep, emission of semen, looking at and touching women, sexual intercourse, lust, anger, greed, delusion, intoxication, envy, injury and the like, ever eager to serve, he should perform acts dear and beneficial to his teacher.
Free of hatred, agreeable in speech and thought, he speaks what is pleasant and true.
Even when distressed he should not utter what is untrue, unpleasant, or blameworthy.
Avoiding honey, meat, fish, juices, sour fermented food and other forbidden food, having performed the practice of begging, permitted by his teacher he should eat the begged food.
He should not utter the name of his teacher, an elder, or one consecrated for sacrifice.
In the absence of the teacher, he performs his duties toward the teacher's son as toward the teacher.
The <s>brahmacārīs</s> are of four kinds: the <s>gāyatra</s>, the <s>brāhma</s>, the <s>prājāpatya</s>, and the <s>naiṣṭhika</s>.

body.text: gāyatra.upanayanād ūrdhvaṃ tri.rātramakṣāra.lavaṇa.aśī gāyatrīm \adhītya-ā sāvitra.vrata.samāpter atra vratacārī.
body.translated_text: From the <s>gāyatra</s> initiation onward, for three nights eating no salt or pungent food, having studied the <s>Gāyatrī</s>, until the completion of the <s>sāvitra</s> vow he is a vow-observer therein.

body.text: brāhmaḥ sāvitra.vratād ūrdhvamanabhiśasta.apatitānāṃ gṛhasthānāṃ gṛheṣu bhaikṣa.ācaraṇaṃ veda.vratacaraṇaṃ ca \kṛtvādvādaśa samā viṃśati samā vā guru.kule \sthitvā vedān vedau vedaṃ vā sūtra.sahitamadhyayanaṃ \kṛtvā gārhasthya.anusaraṇaṃ \kuryāt.
body.translated_text: The <s>brāhma</s>, from the <s>sāvitra</s> vow onward, having performed begging in the houses of unblamed and unfallen householders and the observance of the Vedic vow, having dwelt for twelve years or twenty years in his teacher's house and having studied the <s>Vedas</s>, two <s>Vedas</s>, or one <s>Veda</s> together with the <s>Sūtra</s>, should proceed to the householder's life.
The <s>prājāpatya</s>, having bathed, of the character of daily duties and celibacy, devoted to <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, having investigated the meaning of the <s>Vedas</s> and <s>Vedāṅgas</s>, takes a wife.
The seers say that in the <s>prājāpatya</s> state one should not remain beyond three years.

body.text: naiṣṭhikaḥ kāṣāyaṃ dhātu.vastram ajinaṃvalkalaṃ vā paridhāya jaṭī śikhī vā mekhalī daṇḍī sūtra.ajina.dhārībrahmacārī śucir a.kṣāra.lavaṇa.āśī yāvad ātmano viprayogas tāvad guru.kule \sthitvānivedita.bhaikṣa.bhojī \bhavati.
body.translated_text: The <s>naiṣṭhika</s>, having clothed himself in an ochre dyed garment, antelope-skin, or bark, wearing matted hair or a tuft, with girdle, staff, thread and antelope-skin, a celibate student, pure, eating no salt or pungent food, dwells in his teacher's house as long as he is not separated from the body, eating unannounced begged food.

body.text: dārān saṃgṛhya gṛhastho-apisnānādi.niyama.ācāro nityam aupāsanaṃ \kṛtvā pākayajña.yājī vaiśvadeva.homānte gṛha.āgataṃ guruṃsnātakaṃ ca \pratyutthāya-\abhivandya-āsana.pādya.ācamanāni pradāyaghṛta.dadhi.kṣīra.miśraṃ madhuparkaṃ ca dattvā-annādyair yathāśakti \bhojayati.
body.translated_text: Having taken a wife, the householder too, observing the rules beginning with bathing, daily performing the <s>aupāsana</s> (domestic fire offering), a performer of the cooked oblations, at the end of the <s>vaiśvadeva</s> offering, rising to meet a teacher, an initiated graduate, or a guest who has come to his house, saluting him and offering a seat, water for the feet, and water for sipping, giving the <s>madhuparka</s> (honey-mixture) mixed with ghee, curd, and milk, he feeds him with food according to his ability.

body.text: bhikṣūn brahmacāriṇo-atithīn vedavidaḥ śrotriyān pitṛvya.ācārya.ṛtvij.mātula.śvaśura.ādīn abhyāgatān bāla.vṛddhān anātha.ārta.adhvaśrāntāṃś ca yathārthaṃ \pūjayaty.
body.translated_text: He duly honors mendicants, <s>brahmacārīs</s>, guests, knowers of the <s>Veda</s>, <s>Śrotriyas</s> (learned in scripture), paternal uncles, teachers, officiating priests, maternal uncles, fathers-in-law and the like who have come, as well as the young, the old, the helpless, the afflicted, and those wearied by travel.
Even when unable, having given the first portion or alms together with water, he should eat the remainder.

body.text: dayā.satya.śauca.ācāra.yutaḥsvādhyāya.tarpaṇābhyām ṛṣīn yajñna.bali.homa.jala.puṣpa.ādyair devān śrāddhaiḥ putraiś ca pitṛṛnbalinā bhūtān annādyair manuṣyāṃś ca nityam \arcayed.
body.translated_text: Endowed with compassion, truthfulness, purity, and good conduct, he should daily worship the seers with private recitation and libation, the gods with sacrifice, offering, oblation, water, flowers and the like, the ancestors with <s>śrāddhas</s> (funerary offerings) and with sons, the spirits with offerings, and human beings with food.

body.translated_text: Freed from the three debts, he becomes debtless. Householders are of four kinds: the one of livelihood by trade, the <s>śālīna</s>, the <s>yāyāvara</s>, and the <s>ghorācārika</s>. The one of livelihood by trade lives by agriculture, cattle-keeping, and commerce. The <s>śālīna</s>, endowed with the observances, having sacrificed with cooked oblations and established the fires, is a performer of the new-moon and full-moon sacrifices every fortnight, a performer of the four-monthly sacrifices every four months, a performer of the animal sacrifice every six months, and a performer of the <s>soma</s> sacrifice every year. The <s>yāyāvara</s> sacrifices and causes others to sacrifice with the <s>haviryajñas</s> (oblation sacrifices) and the <s>somayajñas</s> (soma sacrifices), studies and teaches, gives and receives gifts; devoted to the six acts, he ever performs the tending of the fire and provides food to guests and visitors. The <s>ghorācārika</s>, endowed with the observances, sacrifices but does not officiate, studies but does not teach, gives but does not receive; he lives by gleaning, devoted to <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>; offering the <s>agnihotra</s> at evening and dawn, in the months of Mārgaśīrṣa and Jyeṣṭha he undertakes the sword-blade vow and performs the tending of the fire with forest herbs.

body.text: gṛhasthaḥ sa.patnīkaḥ pañcāgnibhis tretāgnibhirvā gṛhād vana.āśramaṃ \yāsyann āhita.agnir anāhita.agniś ca-aupāsanam araṇyām\āropya gṛhe \mathitvā śrāmaṇakīya.vidhānena-\ādhāya-āghāraṃ \hutvāśrāmaṇaka.agnim \ādāya tṛtīyam āśramaṃ \gacchet).
body.translated_text: The householder, together with his wife, intending to go from the home to the forest <s>āśrama</s> with the five fires or the three fires—whether one who has established the sacred fires or one who has not—having deposited the <s>aupāsana</s> fire in the kindling-wood of the <s>araṇī</s>, having churned it out at home and established it by the <s>śrāmaṇaka</s> ordinance, having offered the <s>āghāra</s> oblation, taking the <s>śrāmaṇaka</s> fire, should go to the third <s>āśrama</s>.
As before, he should perform the rites beginning with the laying-out, sprinkling, and tracing of the fire-altar.

body.text: tṛtīyām api vediṃ \parimṛjya ṣaḍ.aṅgula.agnerdarbhair grathite-adhas tridhā.kṛtaṃ rajjuvat- mūle baddhaṃ ṣaṭtriṃśad aṅgula.pramāṇaṃparistaraṇa.kūrcaṃ kṛtvā madhyavedyāṃ \paristṛṇāti) śrāmaṇakaṃ.
body.translated_text: Having wiped the third altar too, having made, six finger-widths from the fire, a strewing-bundle bound with <s>darbha</s> grass, threefold below like a rope, tied at the base, measuring thirty-six finger-widths, he strews the middle altar—this is the <s>śrāmaṇaka</s>.

body.text: śrāmaṇaka.yajñaṃ yajñadaivaviśvān devānity-antam \āvāhya-ājyaṃ nirūpya śrāmanakāya svāhā śrāmaṇaka.yajñāya svāhāyajñadaivataviśvebhyo devebhyaḥ svāhā-ity antaṃ \hutvā caruṃ \juhuyād) ity ādhāra.viśeṣaḥ.
body.translated_text: The <s>śrāmaṇaka</s> sacrifice: having invoked, ending with the formula "to the All-Gods, the deities of the sacrifice," having designated the ghee, having offered, ending with "<s>svāhā</s> to the <s>śrāmaṇaka</s>, <s>svāhā</s> to the <s>śrāmaṇaka</s> sacrifice, <s>svāhā</s> to the All-Gods who are the deities of the sacrifice," he should offer the <s>caru</s> (cooked oblation)—this is the particular ground-rite.
And the upper altar of the <s>śrāmaṇaka</s> fire is thirty-two finger-widths long and four finger-widths wide and raised.
The middle one, surrounding it, is five finger-widths wide and four finger-widths high.
Below, of the breadth and height of the upper altar, is the third altar.

body.text: dvādaśa.aṅgulaṃ madhye nimnaṃ tri.vedi.sahitaṃkuṇḍaṃ kṛtvā-\ādhāya vanastho nityam aupāsanavat sāyaṃ.prātar.āhutīr \hutvā mahāvyāhṛtibhiḥ śrāmaṇaka.agniṃ \juhuyād).
body.translated_text: Having made a pit twelve finger-widths deep in the middle, joined with the three altars, and established the fire, the forest-dweller, daily like the <s>aupāsana</s> rite, offering the oblations at evening and dawn, should offer the <s>śrāmaṇaka</s> fire with the <s>mahāvyāhṛtis</s> (great utterances).
He who has a wife should go to the forest with his wife but without the fires.
The <s>vānaprasthas</s> (forest-dwellers) are those with a wife and those without a wife.
Those with a wife are of four kinds.
The <s>audumbara</s>, the <s>vairiñca</s>, the <s>vālakhilya</s>, and the <s>phenapa</s>.

body.text: audumbaro-akṛṣṭa.phala.avāpya.oṣadhi.bhojī mūla.phala.āśī vāaṇa.hiṅgu.laśuna.madhu.matsya.māṃsa.pūtyanna.dhānya.amla.parasparśana.parapāka.varjī deva.ṛṣi.pitṛ.manuṣya.pūjī vana.caro grāma.bahiṣkṛtaḥsāyaṃ.prātar.agnihotraṃ \hutvā śrāmaṇaka.agni.homaṃ vaiśvadeva.homaṃ \kurvaṃs tapaḥ \samācarati).
body.translated_text: The <s>audumbara</s>, eating unplowed fruits and gathered herbs, or living on roots and fruits, avoiding asafoetida, garlic, honey, fish, meat, foul food, sour grain, the touch of another, and food cooked by another, honoring the gods, seers, ancestors, and human beings, roaming the forest, banished from the village, offering the <s>agnihotra</s> at evening and dawn, performing the <s>śrāmaṇaka</s> fire-oblation and the <s>vaiśvadeva</s> oblation, practices austerity.
Some say he offers having established the <s>śrāmaṇaka</s> fire alone.

body.text: vairiñcaḥ prātryāṃ diśaṃ \prekṣate tāṃ diśaṃ\gatvā tatra priyaṅgu.yava.śyāmāka.nīvāra.ādibhir labdhaiḥ svakīyān atithīṃś capoṣayitvā-agnihotra.śrāmaṇaka.vaiśvadeva.homī nārāyaṇa.parāyaṇas tapaḥ.śīlo\bhavati).
body.translated_text: The <s>vairiñca</s> looks toward the eastern direction; having gone in that direction, having nourished there his own guests with what is obtained—<s>priyaṅgu</s>, barley, <s>śyāmāka</s>, wild rice and the like—a performer of the <s>agnihotra</s>, <s>śrāmaṇaka</s>, and <s>vaiśvadeva</s> oblations, devoted to <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, he becomes of austere character.

body.text: vālakhilyo jaṭā.dharaścīra.valkala.vasano-arka.agniḥ kārttikyāṃ paurṇamāsyāṃ puṣkalaṃ bhuktam \utsṛjya-anyathā śeṣān māsān upajīvyatapaḥ \kuryāt).
body.translated_text: The <s>vālakhilya</s>, wearing matted hair, clothed in rags and bark, having the sun as his fire, having on the full-moon day of Kārttika eaten his fill, casting that off, lives for the remaining months otherwise and performs austerity.
They declare that for him the sun alone is the fire.

body.text: phenapa ud.daṇḍaka unmattako nirodhakaḥ śīrṇa.patita.pattra.āhārī cāndrāyaṇa.vrataṃ caran pṛthivī.śāyīnārāyaṇaṃ \dhyāyan mokṣam eva \prārthayate).
body.translated_text: The <s>phenapa</s>, with raised staff, mad, restraining, eating withered and fallen leaves, observing the <s>cāndrāyaṇa</s> vow, sleeping on the ground, meditating on <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, prays for liberation alone.
Those without a wife are of many kinds.

body.translated_text: It is known that they are of various practices: those eating at fixed times, those with raised staff, those who pound with stones, those whose fruits are lofty, those who use their teeth as a mortar, those living by gleaning, those living by what is in sight, those living like pigeons, those grazing like deer, those who take with the hand, those subsisting on rock-fruit and the like, those eating what is scorched by the sun, those eating <s>bilva</s> fruit, those eating flowers, those eating pale leaves, those eating at intervals of time, those eating once a day, those eating at four times, those lying on thorns, those sitting in the hero's posture, those lying amid five fires, those eating smoke, those lying on stones, those who immerse themselves, those dwelling in water-pots, those keeping silence, those with heads downward, those facing the sun, those with arms upraised, and those standing on one foot.

body.text: atha bhikṣukā mokṣa.arthinaḥ kuṭīcakābahu.udakā haṃsāḥ paramahaṃsāś ca-iti caturvidhā \bhavanti).
body.translated_text: Now the mendicants who seek liberation are of four kinds: the <s>kuṭīcaka</s>, the <s>bahūdaka</s>, the <s>haṃsa</s>, and the <s>paramahaṃsa</s>.

body.text: tatra kuṭīcakā gautama.bhāradvāja.yājñavalkya.hārīta.prabhṛtīnām āśrameṣv aṣṭau grāsāṃṣ caranto yogamārga.tattvajñā mokṣam eva\prārthayante).
body.translated_text: Among them, the <s>kuṭīcakas</s>, taking eight mouthfuls in the hermitages of <s>Gautama</s>, <s>Bhāradvāja</s>, <s>Yājñavalkya</s>, <s>Hārīta</s> and the like, knowers of the truth of the path of <s>yoga</s>, pray for liberation alone.

body.text: bahu.udakās tridaṇḍa.kamaṇḍalu.kāṣāya.dhātu.vastra.grahaṇa.veṣa.dhāriṇo brahmarṣi.gṛheṣu ca-anyeṣu sādhu.vṛtteṣu māṃsa.lavaṇa.paryuṣita.annaṃ varjayantaḥ sapta.agāreṣubhaikṣaṃ \kṛtvā mokṣam eva \prārthayante).
body.translated_text: The <s>bahūdakas</s>, wearing the garb marked by the triple staff, water-pot, and ochre dyed garment, avoiding meat, salt, and stale food in the houses of <s>brahmarṣis</s> and of others of good conduct, having begged in seven houses, pray for liberation alone.

body.text: haṃsā nāma grāme ca-ekarātraṃ nagarepañcarātraṃ vasantas tad.upari na vasanto gomūtra.gomaya.āhāriṇo vā māsa.upvāsino vānitya.cāndrāyaṇa.vratino nityam utthānam eva \prārthayante).
body.translated_text: Those called <s>haṃsas</s>, dwelling one night in a village and five nights in a town but not staying beyond that, subsisting on cow's urine and cow-dung, or fasting for a month, or ever observing the <s>cāndrāyaṇa</s> vow, ever pray for spiritual elevation alone.

body.text: paramahaṃsā nāma vṛkṣa.ekamūle śūnya.agāreśmaśāne ā vāsinaḥ sa.ambarā dig.ambarā vā.
body.translated_text: Those called <s>paramahaṃsas</s> dwell at the single root of a tree, in an empty house, or in a cremation ground, either clothed or naked.
For them there is no duality of righteousness and unrighteousness, truth and falsehood, purity and impurity, and the like.
Regarding all as equal, their selves directed toward all, regarding a clod and gold alike, they perform begging among all the <s>varṇas</s>.

body.text: brāhmaṇānāṃ cāturāśramyaṃ kṣatriyāṇāṃtraya.āśramyaṃ vaiśyānāṃ dvi.āśramyaṃ vihitaṃ.
body.translated_text: The four <s>āśramas</s> are ordained for the <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>, the three <s>āśramas</s> for the <s>Kṣatriyas</s>, and the two <s>āśramas</s> for the <s>Vaiśyas</s>.

body.text: tat.phalaṃ hi sa.kāmaṃ niṣ.kāmaṃ ca-iti dvividhaṃ\bhavati).
body.translated_text: For its fruit is twofold: with desire and without desire.

body.text: sa.kāmaṃ nāma-iha saṃsāre-abhivṛddhiṃ \jñātvā putra.lābha.ādi.abhikāṅkṣaṇam anyat svarga.ādi.phala.kāṅkṣaṇaṃ vā.
body.translated_text: "With desire" means, knowing the prosperity in this worldly existence, the longing for the gaining of a son and the like, or the longing for the fruit of heaven and the like.
"Without desire" means the performance as prescribed, longing for nothing whatever.

body.text: tatra niṣ.kāmam dvividhaṃ bhavati pravṛttirnivṛttiś ca-iti.
body.translated_text: Therein, the desireless is of two kinds: <s>pravṛtti</s> (active engagement) and <s>nivṛtti</s> (withdrawal).

<s>Pravṛtti</s> means: disregarding worldly existence, resorting to the knowledge of <s>sāṃkhya</s>, endowed with <s>prāṇāyāma</s> (breath-control), <s>āsana</s> (posture), <s>pratyāhāra</s> (withdrawal of the senses), and <s>dhāraṇā</s> (concentration), having mastered the breath, attaining the lordly powers beginning with <s>aṇimā</s> (minuteness).

body.text: tat punar api tapaḥ.kṣayāj janma.prāpakatvādvyādhi.bāhulyāc ca na-\ādriyante) paramarṣayo.
body.translated_text: But again, because of the decay of austerity, because it leads to rebirth, and because of the abundance of disease, the supreme seers do not esteem it.

body.text: nivṛttir nāma lokānām anityatvaṃ \jñātvā paramātmano-anyan na kiñcid asti-iti saṃsāram \anādṛtya \cchitvā bhāryā.mayaṃ pāśaṃjita.indriyo \bhūtvā śarīraṃ \vihāya kṣetrajña.paramātmanor yogaṃ \kṛtvā-atīndriyaṃsarvajagad.bījam aśeṣa.viśeṣaṃ nitya.ānandam amṛta.rasa.pānavat sarvadā tṛpt.karaṃ paraṃ jyotiḥpraveśakam iti \vijñāyate).
body.translated_text: <s>Nivṛtti</s> (withdrawal) is: having known the impermanence of the worlds, that there is nothing whatever other than the supreme <s>Ātman</s>, disregarding worldly existence and severing it, having conquered the snare consisting of one's wife, having become one whose senses are subdued, having abandoned the body, having effected the union of the <s>kṣetrajña</s> (knower of the field) with the supreme <s>Ātman</s>—it is known as that which leads to entry into the supreme light, beyond the senses, the seed of the whole world, free of all particularity, eternally blissful, ever giving satisfaction like the drinking of the nectar of immortality.

body.text: nivṛtti.ācāra.bhedādd-hi yoginas trividhā\bhavanti) sāraṅgā eka.arthyā visaragāś ca-iti.
body.translated_text: For, by the difference in the practice of <s>nivṛtti</s>, the <s>yogins</s> become of three kinds: the <s>sāraṅgas</s>, the <s>ekārṣyas</s>, and the <s>visaragas</s>.

body.text: a.nirodhakā nirodhakā mārga.gā vimārga.gāśca-iti caturvidhā sāraṅgā.
body.translated_text: The <s>sāraṅgas</s> are of four kinds: the non-restrainers, the restrainers, the path-goers, and the wrong-path-goers.

body.text: dūra.gā adūra.gā bhrūmadhya.gā a.saṃbhaktāḥsaṃbhaktāś ca-ity eka.arthyāḥ pañcadhā \bhavanti).
body.translated_text: The <s>ekārṣyas</s> (those of one seer) are of five kinds: the far-goers, the near-goers, the goers to the middle of the brows, the non-partakers, and the partakers.
The <s>visaragas</s> are without number.

body.text: tatra sāraṅgāḥ sāraṃ kṣetrajñas taṃ\gacchanti)-iti sāraṅgās teṣv a.nirodhakā ahaṃ viṣṇur iti \dhyātvā ye \caranti) teṣāṃprāṇāyāma.ādayo na \santi).
body.translated_text: Among these, the <s>sāraṅgas</s> are those who go to the essence (<s>sāra</s>), which is the <s>kṣetrajña</s>; hence they are called <s>sāraṅgas</s>. Among them, the non-restrainers, who roam having meditated "I am <s>Viṣṇu</s>," have no <s>prāṇāyāma</s> and the rest.

body.text: ye tu nirodhakās teṣāṃ prāṇāyāma.pratyāhāra.dhāraṇā.ādayaḥ ṣoḍaśa kalāḥ \santi).
body.translated_text: But those who are restrainers have the sixteen parts beginning with <s>prāṇāyāma</s>, <s>pratyāhāra</s>, and <s>dhāraṇā</s>.

body.text: ye mārga.gās teṣāṃ ṣaḍ eva prāṇāyāma.ādayo.
body.translated_text: Those who are path-goers have only the six beginning with <s>prāṇāyāma</s>.

body.text: ye vimārgās teṣāṃ yama.niyama.āsana.prāṇāyāma.pratyāhāra.dhāraṇā.dhyāna.samādhayaśca-ity aṣṭa.aṅgān \kalpayanto dhyeyam apy anyathā \kurvanti).
body.translated_text: Those who are wrong-path-goers, devising the eight limbs—<s>yama</s>, <s>niyama</s>, <s>āsana</s>, <s>prāṇāyāma</s>, <s>pratyāhāra</s>, <s>dhāraṇā</s>, <s>dhyāna</s>, and <s>samādhi</s>—make even the object of meditation otherwise.
Now the <s>ekārṣyas</s>.
Those for whom there is one and the same seer are the <s>ekārṣyas</s>.

body.text: teṣu ye dūra.gās teṣām ayaṃ mārgaḥ.
body.translated_text: Among them, for the far-goers this is the path.

body.text: piṅgalayā nāḍikayā-āditya.maṇḍalam \anupraviśyatatra.sthena puruṣeṇa \saṃyujya tataś candra.maṇḍalaṃ tatra.sthena puruṣeṇa tatovidyutaṃ tatra.sthena puruṣeṇa punaḥ krameṇa vaikuṇṭha.sāyujyaṃ \yanti).
body.translated_text: Having entered the orb of the sun by the <s>piṅgalā</s> channel and united with the <s>Puruṣa</s> abiding there, then the orb of the moon with the <s>Puruṣa</s> abiding there, then the lightning with the <s>Puruṣa</s> abiding there, again in due order they go to union with <s>Vaikuṇṭha</s>.
For the near-goers this is the practice.

body.text: kṣetrajña.paramātmanor yogaṃ kṣetrajña.dvāreṇa\kārayitvā tatra-eva samasta.vināśaṃ dhyātvā-ākāśavat sattā.mātro-aham iti \dhyāyanti).
body.translated_text: Having caused the union of the <s>kṣetrajña</s> with the supreme <s>Ātman</s> by means of the <s>kṣetrajña</s>, having meditated there itself upon the total dissolution, they meditate: "Like space, I am mere existence."

body.text: bhrūmadhya.gāḥ kṣetrajña.paramātmanor yoge sattva.rūpa.agni.dvāreṇa bhrūmadhyaṃ nītvā pañcabhyo-aṅgṣṭa.ādibhyaḥsthānebhya-ākarṣaṇaṃ punaḥ piṅgalā.dvāreṇa niṣkramaṇaṃ pralaya.antaṃkṣetrajña.yogāntaṃ vā \kurvanti).
body.translated_text: The goers to the middle of the brows, in the union of the <s>kṣetrajña</s> with the supreme <s>Ātman</s>, having led it to the middle of the brows by means of the fire whose form is <s>sattva</s>, perform the drawing in from the five places beginning with the great toe, and again the going forth by means of the <s>piṅgalā</s>, ending in dissolution or ending in the union of the <s>kṣetrajña</s>.
Those called non-partakers perform meditation with the mind.
They hear with the ear the scripture that expounds it.
They see with the eye the form of the deity.
They experience the fragrance with the nose.
They make salutation to the deity with the hand.

body.text: saṃbhaktā nāma brāhmaṇaḥ sarva.vyāpakatvādyuktam ayuktaṃ yo-asau paramātmā tat sa vyāpya-ākāśavat \tiṣṭhati).
body.translated_text: The partaker is the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> who, because of the all-pervadingness of that supreme <s>Ātman</s>, who is both fit and unfit, pervading it, abides like space.
Therefore he attains the self as nothing anywhere other than <s>Brahman</s>.
It is said that even for the goer to the middle of the brows there is, from doubt, mere absence of authority.
Therefore nothing other than and distinct from <s>Brahman</s> is established.
Because of moving in manifold ways, because of manifold views, and because of going by wrong paths, they are the <s>visaragas</s>.
Of old, <s>Prajāpati</s>, in order to conceal the teaching, beheld the doctrine of the <s>visaragas</s>.

body.text: taṃ dṛṣṭvā munayo-api mohaṃ \jagmuḥ) kiṃ punar manuṣyāḥ.
body.translated_text: Beholding it, even sages fell into delusion; how much more human beings.
For the beast-like <s>visaragas</s> endowed with egotism, liberation comes in other births, not in this birth.
Therefore the doctrine of the <s>visaragas</s> is not to be practiced.

body.text: kecid visargāḥ kāya.kleśāt kecin mantra.japātkecid yena kenacid dhyānena kecid yena kenacid akṣareṇa kecid vāyu.jayād anye paramātmanākṣetrajaṃ saṃyojya \dhyāyanty) ete paramātma.saṃyogam eva na-\icchanti).
body.translated_text: Some <s>visaragas</s>, by bodily mortification, some by the muttering of <s>mantras</s>, some by some meditation or other, some by some syllable or other, some by conquest of the breath, and others uniting the <s>kṣetrajña</s> with the supreme <s>Ātman</s>—they meditate but do not desire the very union with the supreme <s>Ātman</s>.
They say the <s>Puruṣa</s> abides in the heart alone.

body.text: kecin na kiñcid dhyānam itiyathā.ukta.anuṣṭhānaṃ yogam iti jñātvā muktim \icchanti).
body.translated_text: Some, knowing that practice as prescribed without any meditation is <s>yoga</s>, desire liberation.
For those beast-like <s>visaragas</s>, liberation comes in the intervening births, not in this birth.
For one who longs for release in this very birth, the doctrine of the <s>visaragas</s> is not to be practiced.

body.text: sa.guṇe brahmaṇi buddhiṃ niveśyapaścāt-nir.guṇaṃ brahma-āśritya yatnaṃ kuryād iti \vijñāyate).
body.translated_text: It is known that, having fixed the intellect upon the qualified <s>Brahman</s>, afterward, resorting to the unqualified <s>Brahman</s>, one should make effort.
Now the rule of the <s>śrāmaṇaka</s> for the forest-dweller.

body.text: gṛhasthaḥ somayājī putraṃ pautraṃ ca dṛṣṭvātat.putra.ādīn gṛhe saṃsthāpya mauṇḍyaṃ kṛtvā prājāpatyaṃ kṛcchraṃ \caret).
body.translated_text: The householder who is a performer of the <s>soma</s> sacrifice, having seen a son and a grandson, having established that son and the rest in the home, having shaved his head, should perform the <s>prājāpatya kṛcchra</s> (penance dedicated to Prajāpati).
In spring, in the bright fortnight, in a holy region, together with his wife he goes to the forest <s>āśrama</s>.
On the previous day, having bathed, having made the resolve, having drunk water with <s>kuśa</s> grass, he should keep a fast.
Having offered the <s>aupāsana</s> oblation, with the formula "the fire is your womb," he should deposit it in the <s>araṇī</s> (kindling-wood).

By the ordinance of the new-moon and full-moon sacrifices, gathering the <s>darbha</s> grass and the rest, as before he assembles the strewing-bundles, the enclosing-sticks, the fuel-sticks, the bamboo staff, the sacred thread, the water-pot, the bark-garments, and the like.
By the rule stated before he should make the fire-pit.

body.text: aparasmin divase vaiśvānara.sūktena-agniṃmathitvā prajvālya-agna-\āyāhy)/ upāvaroha-ity agniṃ nidhāya pūrvavat- śrāmaṇaka.agni.āghāraṃ \juhoti).
body.translated_text: On the next day, having churned out the fire with the <s>Vaiśvānara</s> hymn and kindled it, with "O fire, come hither" and "descend," having placed the fire, as before he offers the <s>āghāra</s> oblation of the <s>śrāmaṇaka</s> fire.

body.text: praṇamya-agniṃ pariṣicya-agne prāyaścitte tvam iti pañca.prāyaścittaṃ hutvā-apo.hiraṇya.avamānair ātmānaṃ prokṣyabrahma.daivatyaṃ vaiṣṇavaṃ pañca.vāruṇaṃ ca pradhānān vyāhṛti.antaṃ \yajet).
body.translated_text: Having bowed to the fire and sprinkled it around, having offered the five expiatory oblations with "O fire, you are in expiation," having sprinkled himself with the verses to the waters and to gold, he should sacrifice the principal oblations to <s>Brahman</s> as deity, to <s>Viṣṇu</s>, and the five to <s>Varuṇa</s>, ending with the <s>vyāhṛtis</s>.

body.translated_text: To the west of the fire, having laid two <s>kuśa</s> blades with their tips eastward, having placed a stone above them, with "That excellent (glory) of <s>Savitṛ</s>" he should step upon the stone with the tip of the great toe of the right foot; with "O cows, full of splendor," having put on the bark, the antelope-skin, or the rag, as before he takes the girdle and the rest, the three sacred threads, the upper garment, and the black antelope-skin.

body.translated_text: Having sipped water, with "Hail, O god," having made the circumambulation and salutation of the fire, he should sit.

body.translated_text: With "May the altar be auspicious to us," having sprinkled his own head, having offered the <s>jaya</s> verses, the <s>abhyātāna</s> verses, the <s>rāṣṭrabhṛt</s> verses, and the <s>vyāhṛtis</s>, he should consume the remainder of the ghee with a <s>prāṇāyāma</s>.

body.text: yoge yoga iti dvir ācamya śatam in nu śarada-itipraṇāmam āgantrā samagan mahi-iti pradakṣiṇaṃ ca-ādityasya \kurvīta).
body.translated_text: Having sipped water twice with "In <s>yoga</s> after <s>yoga</s>," he should make a salutation with "For a hundred autumns indeed" and a circumambulation of the sun with "We have fully come."
With "You are the upholder of the kingdom," he should take up the strewing-bundle with its tip upward.

body.text: oṃ bhūs tat savitur oṃ bhuvo bhargo devasyoṃsuvardhiyo yo na iti paccho vyastām oṃ bhūr bhuvas tat savitur oṃ suvardhiyo yo na ity ardharcām oṃ bhūr bhuvaḥ suvas tat savitur iti samastāṃ casāvitrīṃ japtvā vanāśramaṃ praviśya brahmacarya.vrataṃ \saṃkalpayet).
body.translated_text: Having muttered the <s>Sāvitrī</s> verse word by word as "Oṃ bhūs tat savitur, oṃ bhuvo bhargo devasya, oṃ suvar dhiyo yo naḥ," then in half-verses as "oṃ bhūr bhuvas tat savitur, oṃ suvar dhiyo yo naḥ," and then as a whole with "oṃ bhūr bhuvaḥ suvas tat savitur," having entered the forest <s>āśrama</s>, he should resolve upon the vow of celibacy.
And his wife likewise should be a celibate.

body.text: svayam eva-agniṃ pradakṣiṇīkṛtya-ājyena prājāpatyaṃ dhātā.ādīn minda.āhutī vicchinnam aindraṃ vaiśvadevaṃ vaiśṇavaṃ bāhyaṃ viṣṇornuka.ādīn prājāpatya.sūktaṃ tad.vrata.bandhaṃ ca punaḥ pradhānān hutvāprājāpatya.vrataṃ \badhnāti).
body.translated_text: Having himself circumambulated the fire, with ghee he offers to <s>Prajāpati</s> the oblation beginning with <s>Dhātṛ</s>, the <s>minda</s> oblations, the broken <s>aindra</s> oblation, the <s>vaiśvadeva</s>, the <s>vaiṣṇava</s>, the outer one, the oblations beginning with "the strides of <s>Viṣṇu</s>," the <s>prājāpatya</s> hymn, and the binding of that vow; and again, having offered the principal oblations, he binds the <s>prājāpatya</s> vow.

body.text: sthitvā devasya tvā yo me daṇḍa iti dvābhyāṃ pañca.sapta.nava.anyatamaiḥ parvabhir yuktaṃ keśānta.āyataṃvā-apy-avakraṃ vaiṣṇavaṃ dvi.daṇḍam \ādadāti).
body.translated_text: Having stood, with the two verses "To you, the god's..." and "What staff is mine," he takes up a <s>vaiṣṇava</s> double staff furnished with five, seven, or nine—whichever—joints, or one reaching to the end of the hair and unbent.

body.text: yena devā iti kamaṇḍalu.mṛd.grahiṇyau pūrvavadupānaṭ.chatre ca \gṛhṇāty).
body.translated_text: With "By which the gods," he takes up the water-pot and the earth-vessel as before, and the sandals and parasol.

body.translated_text: Having kindled the fires beginning with the <s>gārhapatya</s> and offered the <s>agnihotra</s>, in the <s>āhavanīya</s> fire, with the <s>prājāpatya</s> and the <s>Viṣṇu</s> hymn, having offered everywhere with "<s>svāhā</s> to <s>Agni</s>, <s>svāhā</s> to <s>Soma</s>, to <s>Viṣṇu</s>," he deposits the fires in the <s>araṇī</s>.

body.translated_text: Having laid out the forest <s>āśrama</s> in the forest, on a mountain, in a solitary place, or on a river-bank, he should make the fire-pits as stated.

body.translated_text: Together with his wife, taking the fires, furnished with the vessels and other equipment, he takes up residence in the forest <s>āśrama</s>. Having sprinkled the fire-place, having dug and traced six lines, having placed a fragment of gold and rice-grains, he should deposit the <s>śrāmaṇaka</s> fire.

body.text: vanyān eva pārthivān vānaspatyānkulīra.udghāta.añchaṇān purāṇān kuśa.darbhān ūrṇā.stukāṃ plakṣa.agraṃ sugandhi.tejanaṃ gugguluṃ hiraṇya.śakalān sūrya.kāntaṃ ca \saṃbharati).
body.translated_text: He assembles only forest products—earthen and woody things, crab-clods, gleaned grains, old <s>kuśa</s> and <s>darbha</s> grasses, tufts of wool, a sprig of <s>plakṣa</s>, fragrant reed-grass, <s>guggulu</s> resin, fragments of gold, and a sun-crystal.

body.text: vānaprasthān ṛtvijo vṛtvā-agniṃ mathitvāgārhapatya.ādīṃs tretā.agnīn pañca.agnīn vā-agnyādheya.krameṇa-ādhāya-āhutī dve dvehutvā nityaṃ dvi.kālaṃ vanyair eva \juhoti).
body.translated_text: Having chosen forest-dwelling officiants, having churned out the fire, having established the <s>gārhapatya</s> and the rest, the three fires or the five fires, in the order of the fire-establishment, offering the oblations two by two, he daily offers, at the two times, with forest products alone.

The sage of the forest <s>āśrama</s> practices these ten restraints (<s>niyamas</s>)—bathing, purity, private recitation, austerity, giving, sacrifice, fasting, restraint of the organs, vow-keeping, and silence—and these ten observances (<s>yamas</s>): truthfulness, non-cruelty, uprightness, forbearance, self-control, kindliness, graciousness, gentleness, non-injury, and sweetness.

body.text: bhaktyā viṣṇuṃdhyāyann-agnihotra.śrāmaṇaka.agnihomau dvi.kālaṃ na-utsṛjan grāmya.aśanaṃ tyaktvā vanya.oṣadhīḥ phalaṃ mūlaṃśākaṃ vā nitya.aśanaṃ saṃkalpya tirodhā bhūr ity-āhṛtya- aparāhṇe svayaṃ patnīvā haviṣyam āsrāvitaṃ \pacati).
body.translated_text: Meditating with devotion upon <s>Viṣṇu</s>, not omitting the <s>agnihotra</s> and the <s>śrāmaṇaka</s> fire-oblation at the two times, abandoning village food, resolving as his constant food the forest herbs, fruit, root, or vegetable, having fetched it with "Vanish, O earth," in the afternoon he himself or his wife cooks the sacrificial food, drained of moisture.
At the end of the <s>vaiśvadeva</s>, having fed the guests and those who have come, he eats a measured amount.
He should not eat at night.

body.translated_text: Having spread below <s>darbha</s> grass, grasses, or leaves, a strict vow-observer, apart from his vow-observing wife, he should lie alone.
She performs service to him; he should not approach her.
Free of desire, with semen drawn upward, his senses conquered, he should regard her as a mother.

body.translated_text: He should sacrifice in due succession with forest herbs, as before, the new-moon and full-moon sacrifices, the four-monthly sacrifice, the constellation-offering, and the first-fruits offering.

body.text: mūlaiḥ phalaiḥ pattraiḥ puṣpair vātat.tat.kālena pakvaiḥ svayam eva saṃśīrṇaiḥ prāṇaṃ pravartayann uttara.uttare-apy adhikaṃ tapaḥ.saṃyogaṃphalādi.viśiṣtam \ācared).
body.translated_text: Sustaining his breath by roots, fruits, leaves, or flowers ripened by their respective seasons and themselves fallen, he should practice, in each successively higher stage, a yet greater conjunction of austerity distinguished by fruits and the like.

body.text: atha vā-āhitāgniḥ sarvān agnīn araṇyāmāropya sarvaiḥ saṃvāpa.mantraiḥ pārthivān vānaspatyāṃś ca sarvān samūhyanirmanthya-etena vidhinā-agnim agnyādheya.vidhānena ca mantraiḥ sarvaiḥ sabhyāgny.āyataneśrāmaṇaka.agnim ādhāya-\āharet).
body.translated_text: Or else one who maintains the sacred fires, having deposited all the fires in the <s>araṇī</s>, with all the gathering-<s>mantras</s>, having heaped together all the earthen and woody materials and churned them out, by this rule and by the rule of fire-establishment with all the <s>mantras</s>, having placed the <s>śrāmaṇaka</s> fire in the <s>sabhya</s> fire-place, should bring it forth.
They say the <s>śrāmaṇaka</s> fire is a portion of the <s>sabhya</s> fire.

body.text: a.patnīkaś ca bhikṣuvad agnau homaṃhutvā-araṇyādi.pātrāṇi ca prakṣipya putre bhāryāṃ nidhāya tathā-agnīn ātmany āropyavalkala.upavīta.ādīn bhikṣā.pātraṃ ca saṃgṛhya- an.agnir a.dāro gatvā vane \nivaset).
body.translated_text: And one without a wife, having offered the oblation in the fire like a mendicant, having cast in the <s>araṇī</s> and the other vessels, having deposited his wife with his son, having likewise placed the fires within himself, gathering the bark-garments, the sacred thread, and the rest, and the begging-bowl, fireless and wifeless, having departed, should dwell in the forest.

body.text: tapasāṃ śramaṇam etan mūlaṃ tasmād etadvidhānam enam agniṃ ca śrāmaṇakam ity \āha) vikhanāḥ.
body.translated_text: This is the root of austerities, called <s>śramaṇa</s>; therefore <s>Vikhanas</s> declared this rule, and this fire, to be <s>śrāmaṇaka</s>.

body.text: saṃnyāsa.kramaṃ. saptaty.ūrdhvaṃvṛddho-an.apatyo vidhuro vā janma.mṛtyu.jarā.ādīn vicintya yoga.arthī yadā \syāt) tad.
body.translated_text: The sequence of <s>saṃnyāsa</s>: when one above seventy, aged, without offspring, or a widower, reflecting upon birth, death, old age and the like, becomes a seeker of <s>yoga</s>, then—

body.text: atha vā putre bhāryāṃ nikṣipya paramātmanibuddhiṃ niveśya vanāt saṃnyāsaṃ \kuryāt).
body.translated_text: Or else, having deposited his wife with his son, having fixed his intellect upon the supreme <s>Ātman</s>, he should perform <s>saṃnyāsa</s> from the forest.

body.text: muṇḍito vidhinā snātvā grāmād bāhyeprājāpatyaṃ caritvā pūrvāhṇe tri.daṇḍaṃ śikyaṃ kāṣāyaṃ kamaṇḍalum ap.pavitraṃ mṛd.grahaṇīṃ bhikṣā.pātraṃ ca saṃbhṛtya trivṛtaṃ prāśya- upavāsaṃkṛtvā dine-apare prātaḥ snātvā-agnihotraṃ vaiśvadevaṃ ca hutvā vaiśvānaraṃ dvādaśa.kapālaṃ \nirvapet).
body.translated_text: Having been shaved and bathed according to rule, outside the village having performed the <s>prājāpatya</s> (penance), in the forenoon having assembled the triple staff, the sling, the ochre garment, the water-pot, the water-strainer, the clay-vessel, and the begging-bowl, having eaten the threefold (mixture) and observed a fast, on the next day, having bathed at dawn and offered the <s>agnihotra</s> and the <s>vaiśvadeva</s>, he should offer the twelve-potsherd oblation to <s>Vaiśvānara</s>.

body.text: gārhapatya.agnāv ājyaṃ saṃskṛtya-āhavanīyepūrṇa.āhutī puruṣasūktaṃ ca hutvā-agnaye somāya dhruvāya dhruva.karaṇāya paramātmane nārāyaṇāya svāhā-iti \juhoti).
body.translated_text: Having consecrated the ghee in the <s>gārhapatya</s> fire, in the <s>āhavanīya</s> fire having offered the full oblation and the <s>Puruṣasūkta</s>, he offers with "<s>Svāhā</s> to <s>Agni</s>, to <s>Soma</s>, to the Constant One, to the Maker of constancy, to the Supreme Self, to <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>."

body.text: sruci sruveṇa catur gṛhītaṃ gṛhītvā sarva.agniṣvoṃ svāhā-iti \juhuyād).
body.translated_text: Having taken with the <s>sruva</s> ladle into the <s>sruc</s> ladle a four-fold portion, he should offer in all the fires with "<s>Oṃ</s>, <s>svāhā</s>."
He places the <s>agnihotra</s> oblation-vessel in the <s>āhavanīya</s>, and the vessels other than those made of clay and stone in the <s>gārhapatya</s>.

body.text: gṛhastho-anāhitāgnir aupāsane vanasthaś caśrāmaṇaka.agnau homaṃ hutvā pātrāṇi \prakṣipet).
body.translated_text: A householder who has not established the sacred fires, in the <s>aupāsana</s> fire, and a forest-dweller in the <s>śrāmaṇaka</s> fire, having offered the oblation, should cast in the vessels.

body.text: paccho-ardharcaśo vyastāṃ samastāṃ casāvitrīṃ japtvā bhikṣāśramaṃ praviśāmi-iti taṃ \praviśati).
body.translated_text: Having recited the <s>Sāvitrī</s> foot by foot, half-verse by half-verse, separately and as a whole, with "I enter the <s>āśrama</s> of begging," he enters it.

body.text: antar vedyāṃ sthitvā gārhapatya.ādīn yā teagne yajñiya-iti pratyekaṃ trir āghrāya bhavataṃ naḥ sa.manasāv ity ātmany \āropayet).
body.translated_text: Standing within the altar, having drawn into himself the <s>gārhapatya</s> and the other (fires) with "O <s>Agni</s>, those of yours that are fit for sacrifice," smelling each thrice, he should establish them in himself with "May they be of one mind with us."

body.text: bhūr bhuvaḥ suvaḥ saṃnyastaṃ mayā-iti trirupāṃśu-uccaiś ca praiṣam uktvā dakṣiṇa.hastena sakṛt-jalaṃ pītvā-ācamya tathā-eva-uktvā trir jala.añjaliṃ \visṛjen).
body.translated_text: Having uttered the formula "<s>Bhūḥ</s>, <s>Bhuvaḥ</s>, <s>Suvaḥ</s>, it has been renounced by me" thrice, in a murmur and aloud, having sipped water once with the right hand and rinsed the mouth, uttering it likewise, he should release a handful of water thrice.

body.text: mekhalāṃ catvāry upavītāny ekaṃ vā-upavītaṃkṛṣṇājinam uttarīyaṃ ca pūrvavad \dadāti).
body.translated_text: He gives the girdle, the four sacred threads or the single sacred thread, the black antelope-skin, and the upper garment as before.

body.text: devasya tvā yo me daṇḍaḥ sakhā me gopāya-ititribhis tri.daṇḍaṃ yad asya pāre rajasa iti śikyaṃ yena devāḥ pavitreṇa- ity appavitraṃ yenadevā jyotiṣa-iti kamaṇḍalu.mṛd.grahaṇyāv \ādadīta).
body.translated_text: With "Of the god, you...," "What staff of mine is my friend, protect me," with these three he should take the triple staff; with "What of it is beyond the dust-realm" the sling; with "That strainer by which the gods..." the water-strainer; with "By which light the gods..." the water-pot and the clay-vessel.
Having bathed, he should perform the <s>aghamarṣaṇa</s> (sin-effacing) rite with the <s>Aghamarṣaṇa</s> hymn.

body.text: ācamya ṣoḍaca prāṇāyāmān kṛtvā sahasraṃ śataṃ vā sāvitrīṃ japtvā tathā bhikṣā.pātram alābu dāravaṃ mṛn.mayaṃ vā\gṛhṇāti).
body.translated_text: Having rinsed the mouth and performed sixteen <s>prāṇāyāmas</s> (breath-controls), having recited the <s>Sāvitrī</s> a thousand or a hundred times, he then takes the begging-bowl made of gourd, wood, or clay.

body.text: praṇava.ādy.ādibhiḥ\cf.Cal p.127n.2) pṛthak pṛthak sapta.vyāhṛtibhis tarpayāmi- iti devebhyo jale-adbhis tarpayitvā-ādyābhiś catasṛbhiḥsvadhā-iti pitṛbhyas tarpayet
body.translated_text: Beginning with the <s>praṇava</s> and so forth, with the seven <s>vyāhṛtis</s> (utterances) separately, with "I offer libation," having satisfied the gods with water in water, and having satisfied the ancestors with the first four (utterances) and "<s>Svadhā</s>," he should offer the libation.
He should worship the <s>Āditya</s> (sun) with "Up we (rise) from the darkness."
Having released the handful of water, he should grant freedom from fear to all beings.

body.text: adhyātma.rato yatir bhikṣā.aśī niyama.yamāṃś casamācaran saṃyata.indriyo dhyāna.yogena paramātmānam \īkṣate).
body.translated_text: Delighting in the inner Self, the <s>yati</s> (renunciant), eating begged food and practicing the restraints and observances, his senses controlled, beholds the Supreme Self through the <s>yoga</s> of meditation.
(He follows) the righteous good conduct.

body.text: nivītī dakṣiṇe karṇe yajña.upavītaṃkṛtvā-utkaṭikam āsīno- ahany udaṅ.mukho rātrau dakṣiṇā.mukhas tṛṇair antarite mūtra.purīṣe \visṛjen)-.
body.translated_text: Wearing the sacred thread as a necklace (<s>nivīta</s>) or on the right ear, seated in a squatting posture, by day facing north and by night facing south, he should void urine and excrement over (ground) covered with grass.

body.text: nadyāṃ goṣṭhe pathi chāyāyāṃ bhasmany apsukuśe darbhe vā na- \ācaret).
body.translated_text: He should not do so in a river, a cow-pen, a path, shade, ashes, water, on <s>kuśa</s> grass, or on <s>darbha</s> grass.
He should do it not looking at a cow, a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, water, fire, wind, the sun, stars, or the moon.

body.text: vāma.hastena liṅgaṃ saṃgṛhya-utthāya-udakasyapārśve tathā- āsīno brahmacārī gṛhastho-api śiśne dvir hastayoś ca dvir.dvir gudeṣaṭkṛtvas- mṛdaṃ dattvā-uddhṛtair eva jalaiḥ śaucaṃ \kuryāt).
body.translated_text: Grasping the organ with the left hand and rising, at the side of water, and being likewise seated, the <s>brahmacārī</s>—and the householder too—applying clay twice to the penis and twice to each of the hands and six times to the anus, should perform purification with water drawn out (from the vessel).

body.text: karaṃ vāmaṃ daśa kṛtvaḥ karāv ubhau ca tathāmṛdā-adbhiḥ \prakṣālayet).
body.translated_text: He should wash the left hand ten times and both hands likewise with clay and water.
For the forest-dweller and the mendicant this is twofold.
At night it is as prescribed, or half.

body.text: reto.visarge mūtravat-śaucaṃ kartavyaṃ.retasas trir ity eke.
body.translated_text: On the emission of semen, purification is to be done as for urine; some say thrice for semen.

body.text: sa.upavītī prāṅ.mukha udaṅ.mukhovā-anyatra-āsitvā mṛdā-ambunā pūrvavat pādau pāṇī ca prakṣālya-ācamya mantreṇa- \ācamati).
body.translated_text: Wearing the sacred thread, facing east or facing north, having sat elsewhere, with clay and water as before having washed the feet and hands and rinsed the mouth, he rinses the mouth with the formula.

body.text: brāhmaṇo hṛdgābhiḥ kṣatriyaḥ kaṇṭhagābhir vaiśyastālugābhir adbhir ācāmeta.
body.translated_text: The <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> should sip with water (reaching) the heart, the <s>Kṣatriya</s> with that (reaching) the throat, the <s>Vaiśya</s> with that (reaching) the palate.

body.text: ātmānaṃ prokṣya praty.arkam apo visṛjya-arkaṃ paryety.
body.translated_text: Having sprinkled himself, having released the water toward the sun, he circumambulates the sun.

body.text: udakasya-agner vāma.pārśvaṃ prāṇān āyamyapratyekam oṃ.kārādi.sapta.vyāhṛti.pūrvāṃ gāyatrīm ante sa.śiraskāṃ trir\japet). sa prāṇāyāmas. trīn ekaṃ vā prāṇāyāmaṃ kṛtvā pūtaḥ.
body.translated_text: On the left side of the water and the fire, having restrained the breaths, he should recite each (time) thrice the <s>Gāyatrī</s> preceded by the <s>Oṃkāra</s> and the seven <s>vyāhṛtis</s>, with the head-formula at the end. That is the <s>prāṇāyāma</s>. Having performed three <s>prāṇāyāmas</s> or one, he is purified.

body.text: śataṃ daśa aṣṭau vā sāvitrīṃa sāyaṃ.prātaḥ sandhyām upāsya naiśikam āhnikaṃ ca-eno-\apamṛjyate).
body.translated_text: Having recited the <s>Sāvitrī</s> a hundred, ten, or eight times, worshipping the twilight at evening and dawn, his nightly and daily sin is wiped away.
A twice-born one devoid of the worship of the twilights becomes equal to a <s>Śūdra</s>.
The <s>brahmacārī</s>, proclaiming his own name, should salute with "I, sir, (am so-and-so)."

body.text: śrotre ca saṃspṛśya guroḥ pādaṃ dakṣiṇaṃdakṣiṇena pāṇinā vāmaṃ vāmena vyatyasyar āpādamgṛhṇann ānata.śīrṣo-\abhivādayaty).
body.translated_text: And touching his ears, grasping the teacher's right foot with the right hand and the left with the left, crosswise, down to the feet, with bowed head he salutes.
He should bless him with "May you be long-lived, gentle one."
One who does not pronounce the blessing is not to be saluted.

body.text: mātā pitā gurur vidvāṃsaś ca pratyahamabhivādanīyāḥ.
body.translated_text: Mother, father, teacher, and the learned are to be saluted daily.
Other kinsmen, having returned from abroad, are to be saluted.

body.text: jyeṣṭho bhrātā pitṛvyo mātulaḥ śvaśuraś ca pitṛvat pitṛ.ṣvasā mātṛ.ṣvasā jyeṣṭha.bhharyā bhaginī jyeṣṭhā ca mātṛvatpūjitavyāḥ.
body.translated_text: The eldest brother, the paternal uncle, the maternal uncle, and the father-in-law are to be honored as a father; the paternal aunt, the maternal aunt, the eldest (brother's) wife, and the eldest sister as a mother.

body.text: sarveṣāṃ mātā śreyasī guruś ca śreyān.
body.translated_text: Of all, the mother is more worthy, and the teacher is most worthy.
Not touching another's young wife, he should salute (her) on the ground.
From the saluting of those worthy of salutation come long life, knowledge, strength, health, and auspicious things.
He should not wear the sacred thread, girdle, antelope-skin, and staff worn by another.

body.text: upākṛtya-an.ālasyaḥ śuciḥ praṇava.ādyaṃ vedamadhīyāno-amāvāsyāyāṃ paurṇamāsyāṃ caturdaśyoḥ pratipador aṣṭamyoś ca na-adhīyīta.
body.translated_text: Having begun the study, not lazy, pure, studying the <s>Veda</s> beginning with the <s>praṇava</s>, he should not study on the new-moon and full-moon days, on the fourteenth and first days, and on the eighth days.
In the daily recitation and the oblation there is no suspension of study.

body.text: mārjāra.nakula.maṇḍūka.śva.sarpa.gardabha.varāha.paśu.ādiṣv antarāgateṣv ahorātraṃ sūtaka.pretakayor āśauce tāvat kālaṃ tisro-aṣṭakāsu gurau prete ca trirātram an.adhyāyaḥ \syāt).
body.translated_text: When a cat, mongoose, frog, dog, snake, donkey, boar, cattle and the like come between (teacher and pupil), there should be a suspension of study for a day and night; during the impurity of birth and death for that length of time; for three nights during the three <s>aṣṭakās</s> and when the teacher has died.

body.text: tad.bhāryā.putrayoḥ sva.śiṣyasya ca-uparamemanuṣya.yajñe śrāddha.bhojane ca-ekāham an.adhyāyaḥ syāt āpad.ārtyor aprāyatye.
body.translated_text: On the death of his (the teacher's) wife or son and of one's own pupil, on the human-sacrifice (rite), and at a <s>śrāddha</s>-feast, there should be a suspension of study for one day; in calamity and affliction, while one is unsettled.

body.text: vṛkṣa.nau.yāna.śayaneṣv ārūḍhaḥ prasārita.pādo mūtra.purīṣa.reto.visarge grāme-antaḥśave satya.bhakṣyānna.bhojane chardane śmaṣāna.deśe sandhyā.stanite bhū.kampe dig.dāhe-aśani.ulkā.nipāte rudhira.upala.pāṃsu.varṣe sūrya.indu.rāhu.grahaṇe ca tat tat kāle na-\adhīyīta).
body.translated_text: Mounted on a tree, boat, vehicle, or couch, with feet stretched out, while voiding urine, excrement, or semen, within a village (when) a corpse (is present), while eating consecrated food and ordinary food, while vomiting, in a cremation ground, at twilight, during thunder, an earthquake, a burning of the horizon, the falling of a thunderbolt or meteor, a rain of blood, hail, or dust, and during an eclipse of the sun, moon, or by <s>Rāhu</s>, at each such time he should not study.
The <s>Veda</s>, which brings welfare here and hereafter, is therefore to be studied.
At the end he utters the <s>praṇava</s>, having dismissed (it).

body.text: laukika.agnau samidhau hutvā bhikṣā.annaṃmedhā.pradaṃ śuddhaṃ maunī \bhuñjīta).
body.translated_text: Having offered the two kindling-sticks in the ordinary fire, in silence he should eat the begged food, which is wisdom-bestowing and pure.

body.text: pauṣe māghe vā msāse grāmād bahirjala.ante pūrvavad vratavisarga.homaṃ hutvā svādhyāyam utsṛjya pakṣe śukle vedaṃ kṛṣṇeveda.aṅgaṃ ca yāvad antaṃ samadhītya guror dakṣiṇāṃ dattvā samāvartī\syāt).
body.translated_text: In the month of Pauṣa or Māgha, outside the village at the water's edge, having offered the vow-dismissal oblation as before, having given up the recitation, in the bright fortnight (having studied) the <s>Veda</s> and in the dark fortnight the <s>Vedāṅga</s>, having studied to the end and given the teacher's fee, he may become a returned graduate.

body.text: madhyāhne śuddhe jale mṛd.adbhiḥ pādau hastau cadhāvayitvā-ācamya-aṅgāni saṃśodhya-apaḥ \punantv) iti jale \nimajjed).
body.translated_text: At midday, in pure water, having washed the feet and hands with clay and water and rinsed the mouth, having cleansed the limbs, with "May the waters purify (me)," he should immerse in the water.

body.text: ācānto vaiṣṇavair mantrair viṣṇuṃ hiraṇya.śṛṅgamiti varuṇaṃ ca praṇamya-agha.maṛṣaṇa.sūktena-agha.maṛṣaṇaṃ kṛtvā-idam āpaḥ śivāiti\snāyād). VKḥḍḥṣ 02.13.(130.7-9) āśramiṇaś catvāraḥ snānaṃ nityam evaṃpūrva.uktena vidhinā kāmyaṃ naimittikaṃ ca \kurvanti).
body.translated_text: Having rinsed the mouth, with the <s>Vaiṣṇava</s> formulas saluting <s>Viṣṇu</s> with "The golden-horned one" and <s>Varuṇa</s>, having performed the <s>aghamarṣaṇa</s> rite with the <s>Aghamarṣaṇa</s> hymn, he should bathe with "You waters are auspicious." The four <s>āśramins</s> ever perform bathing thus by the rule stated before, and (also) the optional and occasional (baths).

body.text: dhauta.vastreṇa-āchādya pūrvavad ācamyaprokṣya-āsīnas tiṣṭhan vā kṛta.prāṇāyāmaḥ sāvitrīṃ japtvā-ādityam \upatiṣṭheta).
body.translated_text: Covering (himself) with a washed garment, having rinsed the mouth as before and sprinkled (himself), seated or standing, having performed <s>prāṇāyāma</s>, having recited the <s>Sāvitrī</s>, he should worship the <s>Āditya</s>.

body.text: dakṣiṇa.pāṇinā tīrthena brāhmeṇabhūpati.ādīn daivena nārāyaṇa.adīn kūpya.adīṃś ca-ārṣeṇa viśvāmitra.ādīn paitṛkeṇapitṛ.ādīn adbhis tarpayitvā brahmayajñaṃ kariṣyann ity amiṣe tvā-ūrje tvā-iti yathā.kāmaṃyajuḥ.saṃhitām ādyāṃ strīn anuvākān svādhyāyaṃ \kurvīta).
body.translated_text: With the right hand, by the <s>brahma</s> sacred-spot satisfying <s>Bhūpati</s> and the rest, by the <s>daiva</s> (spot) <s>Nārāyaṇa</s> and the rest, by the <s>kūpya</s> and the rest, by the <s>ārṣa</s> (spot) <s>Viśvāmitra</s> and the rest, by the <s>paitṛka</s> (spot) the ancestors and the rest, having satisfied them with water, with "I shall perform the <s>brahmayajña</s>," with "You for the sap, you for the strength," as he pleases he should perform the recitation of the first <s>Yajuḥ-saṃhitā</s>, three sections (<s>anuvākas</s>).

body.text: naimittikam ṛtaṃ ca satyaṃ ca-ity ādi.sūktānicatur vedādi.mantrān vā-apy \adhīyīta).
body.translated_text: As the occasional (study) he should also study the hymns beginning "The cosmic order and the truth," or the formulas of the four <s>Vedas</s> and the rest.
The <s>brahmayajña</s> is the first of all sacrifices.
Therefore it is to be performed by the twice-born from the time of initiation onward.

body.text: nadyāṃ tīrthe deva.khāte sarasi taṭāke vāsāmānye snānaṃ \kuryāt).
body.translated_text: He should bathe in a river, a sacred ford, a divinely-dug (tank), a lake, or a common reservoir.
In another's water, having drawn out five lumps of clay, he should bathe.
At a well, on its bank, he should sprinkle himself thrice with a pot.

body.text: ucchiṣṭo nagno vā na \snāyāt). tathā na \śayīta).
body.translated_text: Defiled with remnants or naked he should not bathe; likewise he should not sleep (thus).
A sick man should not plunge into the water.

body.text: āturasya snāne naimittike daśa kṛtvo dvādaśakṛtvo vā tam an.āturo jale -avagāhya-ācamya \spṛśet). tataḥ sa pūto \bhavati).

body.translated_text: Having placed both feet or one upon the ground, gracious, with "I sprinkle you, the truth, with reality," he sprinkles in the evening; with "I sprinkle you, the reality, with truth," in the morning.

body.translated_text: Wearing a single garment, lying down, standing, without having bathed, recited, or offered oblation, with feet dry, or facing north, he should not eat.
He should not eat food in a broken vessel, or stale, or placed on a bed, seat, or lap.

Food touched by one defiled with remnants, by an impure person, by one under impurity, or by a fallen one, and (food) during the impurity of birth or death, he should not eat.
Sesame, barley-meal, curd, and parched grain are not to be eaten at night.

body.translated_text: (Food) having worms, hair, or insects, smelled by a cow, or eaten by birds, sprinkled with ashes and water, becomes pure.

body.translated_text: Ever performing the act enjoined in the <s>Śruti</s> and <s>Smṛti</s>, by acts of mind, speech, and body he gradually practices righteousness.

body.translated_text: And in the evening, at the end of the oblation, having fed the guests who have come, having eaten in moderation, he should lie down with his wife.
He should not sleep with wet feet or with his head toward the west or north.
He should approach his own wife on the nights of her fertile season.
At first, for three nights, he should avoid intercourse with the menstruating woman, and sitting and lying together (with her).
He should not unite with another's wife.
From going to another's wife, long life, prosperity, and the splendor of <s>Brahman</s> are destroyed.
He should not eat together with his wife.

Devoted to the welfare of all living beings, he should live by non-injury alone, of pure means, keeping grain in a granary, keeping grain in a pot, or storing nothing for the morrow.
A twice-born should not touch the fallen and the lowest-born.
At sunrise and sunset he should not gaze at the sun.
He should circumambulate the gods, the teacher, the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, ghee, milk, curd, clay, water, fuel-sticks, <s>darbha</s> grass, fire, and trees.

body.translated_text: The path is to be given (yielded) to a returned graduate, a king, a teacher, an eminent person, the sick, a burden-bearer, and a pregnant woman.
Paths are purified by wind, the sun, and (its) rays.

body.translated_text: Into fire, or fire upon fire, fire in a temple, or into water, he should not cast urine, excrement, pus, blood, semen, phlegm, food-remnants, or the scrapings of the limbs.

body.translated_text: He should not look upon another's wife naked, nor (a person) at urine and excrement.
While defiled with remnants he should not gaze at a god, the sun, the moon, a planet, a lunar mansion, or a star.
He should not tread upon the shadow of gods, the teacher, a returned graduate, an initiated person, a king, a cow, or an eminent person.
He should not point out the rainbow to another, nor speak (of it).
He should not awaken one who is sleeping.
He should not travel a road alone.

body.translated_text: He should not drive away a cow grazing in another's field or a calf that is suckling, nor even point (them) out.
He should not be (clothed) in worn-out and soiled garments.
He should avoid play with dice, the smoke of the dead, and the heating of a child (?).
He should not stand upon hair, body-hair, husks, charcoal, potsherds, bones, excrement, urine, pus, blood, semen, phlegm, or food-remnants.
When a limb is smeared with something impure, so long as there is a suspicion in the mind of the smell of that smearing, for that long he should cleanse with clay and water.
He should not dwell together with the fallen, the lowest-born, fools, the irreligious, and enemies.
Defiled with remnants or impure, he should not touch a god, a cow, a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, or fire.
He should not despise nor revile the gods, the <s>Vedas</s>, the king, the teacher, mother and father, and learned <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>.
The despiser and the reviler is destroyed.
He should not perform the reviling or the striking of any living being.

He should not engage in dispute with his teacher, his mother and father, their fathers and the rest, with his brother, paternal uncle, brother, maternal uncle, preceptor, officiating priest, and the like.
Among all purifications of a man, purity of wealth, purity of woman, and purity of food are the most excellent.
Among substances, those made of jewels, gold, and silver he purifies with water, or he touches (them) with fire.

Garments compacted of leather, and vegetables, roots, and fruits, he should sprinkle; small ones he should wash.
Ghee and other substances he should purify and show to a firebrand.

body.translated_text: Silken and woolen things (he purifies) with alkaline earths; cotton cloths with <s>bilva</s> fruits; conch, oyster-shell, and cow's horn with mustard mixed with water; earthen things again by firing; the house by sweeping, plastering, and sprinkling with water; the ground, by digging out and filling with other clay, by a cow's dwelling and the like, and by sweeping and the like, he should purify.
Water on the ground that gives satisfaction to a cow is free of defect and well-purified.
That praised by speech and cleansed by water, (and) the unseen.
A woman's mouth, the artisan's hand, and goods displayed for sale are ever pure.
Fruit that is the remnant of a bird is not to be reproached.
That upon which a gnat or fly has settled, and its droplets, are not defiling.
And that which is touched by the wind, fire, and the sun's rays is pure.

Waters in great quantity are not defiled by urine and excrement.

body.translated_text: The forest-dweller, a constant reciter, should fetch <s>kuśa</s> grass, fuel-sticks and the like for the sake of the fire, and vegetables, roots, and fruits for the sake of food, grown in a pure place.

He should not make a hoard of grain and wealth.
He should not cover (himself) with a (woven) garment.
When (a substance is) called honey he takes water; when called meat, he takes a thing made of flour.

body.translated_text: Without a companion, without fire, without abode, free of doubt, equable in honor and dishonor, free of dispute, anger, greed, delusion, and untruth, outside the village in a solitary hut, in a temple, or at the root of a tree, he should dwell.

body.translated_text: Having joined to the triple staff the ochre garment, the water-strainer and the rest, carrying it at his neck with the left hand, having taken the begging-bowl with the right, at a single time, in the houses of pure <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>, he should go for alms at the end of the <s>vaiśvadeva</s>.

Standing with face downward, he seeks to obtain alms.
Having stood only for the time of milking a cow, or half of that, he should depart.
Even when receiving nothing and even when dishonored, he should not despair; even when honored upon obtaining (alms), he should not be (too) content.
He should not walk quickly or slowly.
Except at the time of begging, he should not go to another's house.
He should not go beyond a <s>krośa</s> to beg.

body.translated_text: With the hand, by the rule of the <s>agnihotra</s>, having resolved upon the self-sacrifice, he should eat food merely sufficient to sustain life, or eight mouthfuls; he should not eat at pleasure.

body.translated_text: Having abandoned attachment, restrained in observances and restraints, speaking what is pleasant and true, not opposed to any living being, ever equable, delighting in the inner self, a practitioner of meditation-<s>yoga</s>, beholding <s>Nārāyaṇa</s> as the supreme <s>Brahman</s>, he should hold the <s>dhāraṇā</s>.

body.translated_text: Having bathed (the body) with the <s>Gāyatrī</s>, having there made it sit or lie down, having laid down upon the right hand the triple staff with the <s>Vaiṣṇava</s> formulas, on the left—with "What is on the far shore of that dust"—the sling and the water-strainer, on the belly with the <s>Sāvitrī</s> the begging-bowl, on the secret part with "Earth (you go) to earth" the ochre garment, the earthen vessel, and the water-pot, having laid (them) down, he should cover (it).

body.translated_text: When a <s>saṃnyāsin</s> who maintained the sacred fires, having placed the fires within himself, has died, having bathed his body with the <s>Gāyatrī</s> and carried it as before, having placed it in a pure region, with "Descend into that fire" lowering that fire into the ordinary fire, with "The strainer is yours" having put ghee and milk into the mouth, having laid down the triple staff and the rest as before, he performs the cremation with the <s>fire-establishing</s> formulas and those (consecrated) fires, by the <s>brahmamedha</s> or the <s>pitṛmedha</s>.
