He performs the <s>Nārāyaṇabali</s>.

body.text: tad.vahanaṃ khanitvā pidhānaṃ dahanaṃnārāyaṇa.baliṃ vā yaḥ \kuryāt)/ so-aśvamedha.phalaṃ \samāpnuyāt).
body.translated_text: He who performs the carrying, the digging, the covering, the cremation, or the <s>Nārāyaṇabali</s> of that (body) attains the fruit of the <s>aśvamedha</s>.

body.text:
nārāyaṇa.baliṃ nārāyaṇād evasarvārtha.siddhir iti brahmaṇa.ādyair narair hatasya-ātma.ghātinorajju.śastra.udaka.aśani.daṃṣṭri.paśu.sarpa.ādibhiḥ sarvapāpa.mṛtasya-adāhyānām anyeṣāṃ bhikṣoś ca-ekādaśa.dinād ūrdhvaṃ mahāpātakināṃ pañcānāṃ dvādaśa.saṃvatsarād ūrdhvaṃsapiṇḍīkaraṇa.sthāne mṛtaka.artham aparapakṣe dvādaśyāṃ śravaṇe vā
\karoti).
body.translated_text: The <s>Nārāyaṇabali</s>—since from <s>Nārāyaṇa</s> alone (comes) the accomplishment of every purpose—he performs at the place of the <s>sapiṇḍīkaraṇa</s>, for the sake of the dead: for one slain by <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> and other men, for a suicide, for one dead of all (manner of evil) by rope, weapon, water, thunderbolt, a tusked animal, cattle, a snake and the like, for the others among the un-cremated, and for a mendicant—after the eleventh day; for the five (kinds of) great sinners—after twelve years—on the twelfth (lunar day) of the dark fortnight, or under the constellation Śravaṇa.
On the previous day he should invite twelve <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>.

body.text: apare-ahani viṣṇor ālaya.pārśve nadī.tīregṛhe vā-agni.āyatanaṃ kṛtvā-āghāraṃ \juhuyād).
body.translated_text: On the next day, beside a temple of <s>Viṣṇu</s>, on a river-bank, or in the house, having made the fire-place, he should offer the <s>āghāra</s> oblation.

body.text: agniṃ paristīrya-agner vāyavyāṃ viṣṭaredarbheṣu tad.rūpaṃ suvarṇaṃ vā saṃsthāpya puruṣaṃ dhyāyann oṃ bhūḥ puruṣam ity -ādyaiḥprāṅ.mukhaṃ devaṃ nārāyaṇam āvāhya-āsana.pādya.ācamanāni \dadyāt).
body.translated_text: Having strewn (the area) around the fire, having established to the northwest of the fire, upon the spread <s>darbha</s> grasses, the form of that (deity) or gold, meditating upon the <s>Puruṣa</s>, with "Oṃ bhūḥ, the Puruṣa" and the rest, having invoked the god <s>Nārāyaṇa</s> facing east, he should give the seat, foot-water, and sipping-water.

Having bathed (the image) with the <s>Puruṣasūkta</s>, or with the eight-syllabled formula "We know <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>," he worships with garment, upper garment, ornament, foot-water, sipping-water, flowers, perfume, incense, lamp, unbroken grains, and sipping-water.
With the twelve names beginning with <s>Keśava</s> he should satisfy (the deity) with waters.

body.text: pariṣicya sahasraśīrṣa.ādyair viṣṇor nuka.ādyairdvādaśa.nāmabhiś ca-ājyaṃ caruṃ \juhuyāt).
body.translated_text: Having sprinkled (the oblation) around, he should offer the ghee and the <s>caru</s> (cooked oblation) with the verses beginning "The thousand-headed one" and with the twelve names of <s>Viṣṇu</s> beginning with "nuka."

body.text: guḍa.ājya.phala.yuktaṃ pāyasaṃ havirviṣṇu.gāyatryā deva.īśāya nivedya pādya.ācamana.mukha.vāsaṃ \dadyāt).
body.translated_text: Having presented to the Lord of gods the <s>pāyasa</s> (milk-rice) oblation joined with molasses, ghee, and fruit, by the <s>Viṣṇu-gāyatrī</s>, he should give water for the feet, water for sipping, and a mouth-perfume.

body.text: agner dakṣiṇe darbheṣu-ūtara.agreṣu dakṣiṇādy\arcayitvā)/ nārāyaṇāya sahasraśīrṣāya sahasrākṣāya sahasrapādāyaparamapuruṣāya paramātmane paraṃjyotiṣe parabrahmaṇe- avyaktāya sarvakāraṇāya yajña.īśvarāyayajñātmane viśvebhyo devebhyaḥ sarvābhyo devatābhyaḥ sādhyebhya-ity antaiḥ pāyasaṃ baliṃ\dattvā)- ājyam ebhir\juhoti).
body.translated_text: To the south of the fire, upon <s>darbha</s> grasses with their tips pointed north, having worshipped toward the south, having given the <s>pāyasa</s> as an offering with (the formulas) ending "to <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, the thousand-headed, the thousand-eyed, the thousand-footed, the Supreme Person, the Supreme Self, the Supreme Light, the Supreme <s>Brahman</s>, the Unmanifest, the Cause of all, the Lord of sacrifice, the Self of sacrifice, to the All-Gods, to all the deities, to the <s>Sādhyas</s>," he offers the ghee with these (formulas).

body.text: brāhmaṇān pādau prakṣālya navānivastra.uttarīya.ābharaṇāni dattvā puṣpa.ādyaiḥ pūjayitvā dvādaśa.mūrtiṃ dhyāyann upadaṃśa.ghṛta.guḍa.dadhi.phala.yuktaṃ śvetam annaṃ bhojayitvāyathā.śakti suvarṇaṃ dakṣiṇāṃ \dadāti).
body.translated_text: Having washed the feet of the <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>, having given new garments, upper garments, and ornaments, having honored them with flowers and the rest, meditating on the twelvefold form, having fed them white food joined with condiments, ghee, molasses, curd, and fruit, he gives gold as the fee according to his ability.
Having praised with the verses beginning "The thousand-headed one," he should bow with the twelve names. He offers the concluding oblation.

body.text: abhīṣṭāṃ parāṃ gatiṃ sa gatvā viṣṇor loke\mahīyate).
body.translated_text: Having attained the desired supreme goal, he is magnified in the world of <s>Viṣṇu</s>.

body.text: cāturvarṇya.saṃkareṇa-utpannānām anuloma.pratiloma.antarāla.vrātyānām utpattiṃ nāma vṛttiṃ ca.-
body.translated_text: (Now) the origin and the livelihood of the <s>anuloma</s>, <s>pratiloma</s>, intermediate, and <s>vrātya</s> (classes), born from the intermixture of the four <s>varṇas</s>.
One born from a higher-born (father) in a lower-born (woman) is an <s>anuloma</s> (with the grain).
One born from a lower-born (father) in a higher-born (woman) is a <s>pratiloma</s> (against the grain).
Then one born from an <s>anuloma</s> in an <s>anuloma</s> woman is an intermediate (<s>antarāla</s>).
One born from a <s>pratiloma</s> in a <s>pratiloma</s> woman becomes a <s>vrātya</s>.

body.text: brahmaṇo mukhād udbhūtā brāhmaṇā brāhmaṇyaś ca brahma.ṛṣayaḥ patnyo \babhūvus).
body.translated_text: From the mouth of <s>Brahman</s> arose the <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> and the <s>Brāhmaṇīs</s>; the <s>brahmarṣis</s> became their wives.

body.text: teṣāṃ gātra.utpannād brāhmaṇyāṃ a.sagotrāyāṃvidhinā sa.mantrakaṃ gṛhītāyāṃ jāto brāhmaṇaḥ śuddho \bhavet).
body.translated_text: From a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> arisen from their body, in a <s>Brāhmaṇī</s> not of the same <s>gotra</s>, taken (in marriage) by rule with the formulas, the one born would be a pure <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>.

body.text: vidhi.hīnam anya.pūrvāyāṃ golakohartṛkāyāṃ kuṇḍaś ca viprau dvau ninditau \syātāṃ ).
body.translated_text: (But) in (a woman) married to another before, devoid of rule, the <s>golaka</s> (born while the husband lives) and the <s>kuṇḍa</s> (born after the husband's death)—these two <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> would be reprehensible.

body.text: tasmād adho bāhubhyāmāt kṣatriyāt kṣatriyāyāṃ vidhivat-jātaḥ kṣatriyaḥ śuddhas.
body.translated_text: Below them, from the arms, from a <s>Kṣatriya</s> in a <s>Kṣatriyā</s>, one born according to rule is a pure <s>Kṣatriya</s>.

body.text: tayor a.vidhikaṃ gūḍha.utpanno-aśuddhobhoja.ākhyo na-eva-\abhiṣecyaḥ). paṭṭa.bandho rājñaḥ saināpatyaṃ \karoti).
body.translated_text: Of those two, one secretly born without rule is impure, called <s>bhoja</s>, and is not to be consecrated (as king); without the fillet-binding (of coronation) he performs the generalship of the king.
In the absence of a pure (heir), without the fillet-binding he should protect the people.
His conduct would be like a king's.

body.text: adhastād ūrubhyāmād vaiśyād vaiśyāyāṃ tathā vaiśyaḥ śuddho.
body.translated_text: Below, from the thighs, from a <s>Vaiśya</s> in a <s>Vaiśyā</s> likewise, (one born) is a pure <s>Vaiśya</s>.
Devoid of rule, the impure one is a jeweller; he would be a piercer of gems, pearls and the like, and a maker of conch-shell bangles.
Now from a <s>Śūdra</s>, born from the feet, in a <s>Śūdrā</s> by rule, the <s>Śūdra</s> is pure.
From an adulterer, the reprehensible <s>Śūdra</s> is the <s>mālavaka</s>, a horse-keeper and a carrier of horse-fodder.
These are the four-<s>varṇa</s> (classes).
All those of theirs born by the (proper) <s>saṃskāra</s> (sacrament) are the <s>anuloma</s> and the rest.
Born from a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> in a <s>Kṣatriya</s> maiden, the equal-class one is the foremost among the <s>anulomas</s>.

body.text: asya vṛttir ātharvaṇaṃkarma.aśva.hasti.ratha.saṃvāhanam ārohaṇaṃ rajñaḥ saināpatyaṃ ca-āyurveda.kṛtyaṃ.
body.translated_text: His livelihood is the <s>Ātharvaṇa</s> rites, the driving of horses, elephants, and chariots, mounting (them), the generalship of the king, and the practice of <s>Āyurveda</s>.
The one secretly born is called <s>abhiniṣikta</s>.

body.text: abhiṣiktaś cet-nṛpo bhūyād aṣṭāṅgam āyurvedaṃbhūta.tantraṃ vā \saṃpaṭet).
body.translated_text: If he be a consecrated king, he should master the eight-limbed <s>Āyurveda</s> or the science of (controlling) spirits.
Of the conduct stated therein, endowed with compassion, truth-speaking, by that ordinance he should do what is beneficial to all living beings.
Or his livelihood is chiefly astronomy, calculation and the like.
From a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> in a <s>Vaiśyā</s> is the <s>ambaṣṭha</s>, who lives by (tending) the enclosure, a fire-dancer, a flag-proclaimer, a surgeon (extractor of darts).

body.text: jarāt kumbhakāraḥ kulāla.vṛttir na-āpito nābherūrdhva.vaptā ca.
body.translated_text: From an adulterer (he is) the potter, of the potter's craft, not a barber, and one who shaves above the navel.

body.text: kṣatriyād vaiśyāyāṃ madguḥ śreṣṭhitvaṃ prāpto mahānarma.ākhyaś ca vaiśya.vṛttiḥ kṣātram karma na-\ācarati).
body.translated_text: From a <s>Kṣatriya</s> in a <s>Vaiśyā</s> is the <s>madgu</s>, who has attained pre-eminence, also called <s>mahānarma</s>, of the <s>Vaiśya</s>'s livelihood; he does not perform the <s>Kṣatriya</s>'s work.
From the secret (union he is) the <s>āśvika</s>, a buyer and seller of horses.

From a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> in a <s>Śūdrā</s> is the <s>pāraśava</s>, whose livelihood is the worship of <s>Bhadrakālī</s>, painting, the science of bodily marks, the sounding of musical instruments, and massage.
Born from an adulterer is the <s>niṣāda</s>, who does the killing of beasts of prey and other game.
From a <s>Kṣatriya</s> (<s>rājanya</s>) in a <s>Śūdrā</s> is the <s>ugra</s>, whose work is the chastising of those well-deserving punishment.
From an adulterer (he is) the <s>śūlika</s>, whose work is torture such as impalement on the stake.
From a <s>Vaiśya</s> in a <s>Śūdrā</s> is the <s>cūcuka</s>, a buyer and seller of areca-nut, betel, sugar and the like.
From the secret (union he is) the <s>kaṭakāra</s>, of the mat-maker's craft.

body.text: tato-anulomād anulomāyāṃ jātaś ca-anulomaḥpitur mātur vā jātaṃ vṛttiṃ \bhajeta).
body.translated_text: Then one born from an <s>anuloma</s> in an <s>anuloma</s> woman, being an <s>anuloma</s>, should follow the livelihood born of his father or mother.

body.text: kṣatriyād viprakanyāyāṃ mantravat- jātaḥ sūtaḥpratilomeṣu mukhyo-ayaṃ mantrahīna.upanīto dvijadharma.hīno.
body.translated_text: Born from a <s>Kṣatriya</s> in a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> maiden, with formulas, is the <s>sūta</s>, foremost among the <s>pratilomas</s>; initiated without formulas, he is devoid of the twice-born's duty.
His livelihood is the proclaiming of righteousness and the preparation of the king's food.

body.text: jāreṇa mantrahīna.jo rathakārodvijatva.vihīnaḥ śūdra.kṛtyo- aśvānāṃ poṣaṇa.damanādi.paricaryā.jīvī.
body.translated_text: By an adulterer, one born without formulas is the <s>rathakāra</s> (chariot-maker), devoid of twice-born status, of <s>Śūdra</s>'s work, living by the service of nourishing, taming and so forth of horses.

body.text: vaiśyād brāhmaṇyāṃ māgadhaḥ. śūdrair apyabhojyān no- aspṛśyaḥ sarvavandī praśaṃsā.kīrtana.gāna.preṣaṇa.vṛttir.
body.translated_text: From a <s>Vaiśya</s> in a <s>Brāhmaṇī</s> is the <s>māgadha</s>; though not untouchable, his food is not to be eaten even by <s>Śūdras</s>; he is a universal bard, his livelihood being praise, recitation of fame, song, and message-carrying.
From the secret (union he is) the <s>cakrī</s>, who would be a seller of salt and oil.

body.text: vaiśyān nṛpāyām āyogavas tantu.vāyaḥ paṭa.kartā vastra.kāṃsya.uapjīvī.
body.translated_text: From a <s>Vaiśya</s> in a <s>Kṣatriyā</s> (royal woman) is the <s>āyogava</s>, a weaver, a maker of cloth, living by garments and bell-metal.
From secret conduct (he is) the <s>pulinda</s>, of forest livelihood, a slayer of wicked beasts and creatures.

body.text: śūdrāt kṣatriyāyāṃ pulkasaḥ kṛtakāṃ vāārkṣāṃ vā surāṃ \hutvā) pācako \vikrīnīta).
body.translated_text: From a <s>Śūdra</s> in a <s>Kṣatriyā</s> is the <s>pulkasa</s>; having distilled artificial or <s>ārkṣa</s> (palm) liquor, as a cook he sells it.
From thieving conduct (he is) the <s>velava</s>, whose work is jugglery, dancing, and song.

body.text: śūdrād vaiśyāyāṃ vaidehakaḥ śūdra.aspṛśyastair apy abhojya.anno vanya.vṛttir aja.mahiṣa.gopālas tad.rasān vikrayī.
body.translated_text: From a <s>Śūdra</s> in a <s>Vaiśyā</s> is the <s>vaidehaka</s>, untouchable to <s>Śūdras</s>, his food not to be eaten even by them, of forest livelihood, a herdsman of goats and buffaloes, a seller of their products.
From theft (he is) the <s>cakrika</s>, living by salt, oil, and oil-cake.

body.text: śūdrād brāhmaṇyāṃ caṇḍālaḥsīsaka.ālāyasa.ābharaṇo vardhrā.bandha.kaṇṭhaḥ kakṣerī.yukto yatas tataś caran sarvakarma.bahiṣkṛtaḥ pūrvāhṇe grāma.ādau vīthyām anyatra-api malāny apakṛṣya bahir \apohayati).
body.translated_text: From a <s>Śūdra</s> in a <s>Brāhmaṇī</s> is the <s>caṇḍāla</s>, with ornaments of lead and black iron, with a leather-bound throat, equipped with a (basket at the) armpit, roaming hither and thither, excluded from all rites; in the forenoon, in the village and elsewhere, in the lane, having drawn out the filth, he removes it outside.
Far outside the village he should dwell with his own kind.
After midday this one does not enter the village.
Should he enter, he is to be put to death by the king.
Otherwise (the king) incurs the (guilt of) slaying an embryo.
And (so too are) the intermediate and the <s>vrātya</s> (classes).

body.text: cūcukād viprāyāṃ takṣako-aspṛśyojhallarī.hasto dārukāraḥ suvarṇakāro-ayaskāraḥ kāṃsyakāro vā.
body.translated_text: From a <s>cūcuka</s> in a <s>Brāhmaṇī</s> is the <s>takṣaka</s> (carpenter), untouchable, with a <s>jhallarī</s> (drum) in hand, a woodworker, or a goldsmith, ironsmith, or bell-metal-smith.
In a <s>Kṣatriyā</s> (is born) the <s>matsyabandhu</s> (kinsman of fishers), a catcher of fish.
In a <s>Vaiśyā</s> would be the <s>sāmudra</s>, living by sea-trade and a slayer of fish.
From an <s>ambaṣṭha</s> in a <s>Brāhmaṇī</s> is the <s>nāvika</s> (boatman), living by sea-trade and fish; he floats the boat for crossing the sea.
In a <s>Kṣatriyā</s> is the lower barber (<s>adhonāpita</s>), who shaves the hair below the navel.
From a <s>madgu</s> in a <s>Brāhmaṇī</s> is the <s>veṇuka</s>, a player of bamboo-flute and lute.
In a <s>Kṣatriyā</s> is the <s>karmakara</s> (laborer), doing labor.
From a <s>vaidehaka</s> in a <s>Brāhmaṇī</s> is the <s>carmakāra</s> (leather-worker), living by leather.
In a <s>Kṣatriyā</s> (royal woman) is the <s>sūcika</s> (tailor), whose work is needle-piercing.
From an <s>āyogava</s> in a <s>Brāhmaṇī</s> is the <s>tāmra</s> (coppersmith), living by copper.
In a <s>Kṣatriyā</s> is the <s>khanaka</s> (digger), living by digging.
From a digger in a <s>Kṣatriyā</s> is the <s>udbandhaka</s>, a <s>Śūdra</s>, untouchable, a washer of garments.
From a <s>pulkasa</s> in a <s>Brāhmaṇī</s> is the <s>rajaka</s> (washerman), a cleanser of the dirt of garments.

body.text: caṇḍālād viprāyāṃ śvapacaḥ caṇḍālavaccihna.yukto nitya.nindyaḥ sarvakarma.bahiṣkāryo nagaryādau mala.apohakaḥ śmaśāne \vasan) heyapātra.grāhī pretam abandhukaṃ \visṛjeta).
body.translated_text: From a <s>caṇḍāla</s> in a <s>Brāhmaṇī</s> is the <s>śvapaca</s>, marked with the signs of a <s>caṇḍāla</s>, ever to be reviled, to be excluded from all rites, a remover of filth in the city and elsewhere; dwelling in the cremation ground, taking discarded vessels, he should dispose of a corpse that has no kinsman.

body.text: vadhyān hatvā tad.vastrādi.grāhīparādhīna.āhāro bhinnapātra.bhojī śvamāṃsa.bhakṣī carma.vāra.vāṇa.vāṇijya.kārī \syāt).
body.translated_text: Having slain those condemned to death, taking their garments and the rest, his food dependent on others, eating from a broken vessel, an eater of dog's flesh, he would be a worker in leather, water-(vessels?), and the selling of (?).

body.text: tasmān nikṛṣṭe sute samutpanne patito naṣṭoghorān narakān \vrajati).
body.translated_text: Therefore, when a degraded son is born, the fallen, ruined one goes to dreadful hells.

body.text: sat.putro narakebhyas trāyakaḥ pitṛṛn\pāvayitvā)/ śubhāṃl lokān \nayati).
body.translated_text: A good son is a deliverer from the hells; having purified the ancestors, he leads them to the auspicious worlds.

body.text: tasmād brāhmaṇādyāḥ savarṇāyāṃ vidhivat putram \utpādayeyur)-iti vikhanāḥ. End of the text.
body.translated_text: Therefore the <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> and the rest should beget a son in an equal-class (wife) according to rule—thus (says) <s>Vikhanas</s>. End of the text.
